newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down on profit-taking, isles row.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down on profit-taking, isles row.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed lower on Monday as market confidence was hampered by psychological resistance and fear of escalating tensions between Taipei and Tokyo, brokers said.
The weighted index ended 24.24 points or 0.36 percent down at 6,620.42. Turnover was an active T$48.50 billion.

Investors showed unwillingess to chase higher prices after the index had climbed to a 19-month high on Saturday. They also worried that tensions would worsen after Taiwan and Hong Kong activists on Monday hoisted Chinese flags on a deserted East China Sea archipelago in a challenge to Japan's sovereignty.

"Investors were cautious about the index's ability to keep rising without interruption following Saturday's record high, and the concerns over political tension merely intensified the caution," said Lin Long-hsien of United Securities.

Electronics, main benefactor of the market's recent bullishness, fell victim to heavy profit-taking and lost 0.97 percent, with BTC dropping T$2.10 or 6.50 percent to T$30.20. Delta Electronic fell by 6.06 percent or T$4 to end at T$62.
"The outlook for the sector is still sound, but for one day investors decided to slow their pace," Lin said.
Brokers said Wall Street's record close on Friday did not have much effect on local sentiment.
They expected the Taiwan market to remain in a consolidation on Tuesday. A 6,590-6,640 range was seen.
